title: Imposes Aluminum Tariffs Under Section 232
description_short: Trump issued Proclamation 9704 imposing 10 percent tariffs on aluminum imports under Section 232.
description_medium: On March 8, 2018, Trump issued Proclamation 9704, imposing a 10 percent tariff on aluminum imports under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act. description_long: Proclamation 9704 applied a 10 percent tariff to covered aluminum imports after the Commerce Department's Section 232 investigation concluded that import levels threatened national security. description_short: Trump pardoned former Army officer Michael Behenna, convicted in a 2008 Iraq killing case.
description_medium: On May 6, 2019, Trump pardoned Michael Behenna, a former Army officer convicted in connection with a 2008 killing in Iraq. The Justice Department's official pardon list records the grant. A pardon is different from a commutation because it forgives the offense rather than simply reducing remaining punishment.
description_long: Michael Behenna's case arose from the 2008 killing of Iraqi detainee Ali Mansur after Behenna questioned him while serving in Iraq. A military jury convicted Behenna of unpremeditated murder in 2009; an appeals court later reduced his sentence, and he was released on parole in 2014. Trump granted the pardon on May 6, 2019. The supplied record describes him as a former Army officer and links the Justice Department pardon list, which confirms the presidential action. The clemency decision drew attention to the relationship between presidential intervention and military justice, particularly in cases involving conduct during war. This entry does not claim the pardon changes historical facts or resolves debate over the conviction. The official list establishes the pardon, while prosecution details belong to the court record. The notes do not provide Trump's full rationale, so no motive is assigned here.
